nceb7d9cc17.headline: China’s Xi says there are ‘no winners’ in tariff war as he visits South-east Asia
nceb7d9cc17.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping said there are no winners in the tariff war while visiting South-east Asia. The input says Donald Trump has kept 145 tariffs on China in place, even as some other tariffs were paused.
nceb7d9cc17.why: China is the world's second-largest economy, and US-China tariffs affect global trade flows, supply chains and corporate earnings across many sectors.

n9b832b32ef.headline: Greece signs deal to buy 16 anti-ship missiles from France
n9b832b32ef.summary: Greece has signed a deal to buy 16 anti-ship missiles from France. The deal is the latest in a series of Greek military equipment purchases from France.
n9b832b32ef.why: Defence procurement contracts from European governments support aerospace and defence suppliers and reflect rising regional military spending.

n09eccc6839.headline: Japan grants Nigeria $30 million for start-up hubs in Abuja
n09eccc6839.summary: The Japan International Cooperation Agency and the Nigerian Federal Government have signed a $30 million agreement for start-up hubs in Abuja. The funding is aimed at Nigeria's digital economy.
n09eccc6839.why: Development finance from bilateral agencies such as JICA supports infrastructure and digital economy growth in emerging markets.

n79ee7c5c6e.headline: How cutting Medicaid would affect long-term care and family caregivers
n79ee7c5c6e.summary: Medicaid is the largest source of funding for long-term care for elderly and disabled Americans. Republican proposals to cut its budget could jeopardise support relied on by families and caregivers.
n79ee7c5c6e.why: Medicaid is a major federal health program, and changes to its budget affect healthcare providers, state finances and the US fiscal outlook.

n383f14d8ad.headline: Meta Faces Historic Antitrust Trial That Could Force It to Break off Instagram, WhatsApp
n383f14d8ad.summary: Meta Platforms faces a historic antitrust trial beginning Monday that could force it to separate Instagram and WhatsApp, startups it bought over a decade ago.
n383f14d8ad.why: Meta owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, and a forced divestiture would reshape one of the largest digital advertising businesses.

impacts.name: Meta Platforms
impacts.why: A court ruling could force the sale or separation of Instagram and WhatsApp, changing Meta's business mix.

n2db2fd55df.headline: South Africa’s rand gains on report ANC may scrap VAT hike
n2db2fd55df.summary: The rand firmed about 1.2% against the dollar to 18.9150 after a report said the ANC may back down on a planned VAT hike, alongside broader dollar weakness.
n2db2fd55df.why: The rand is South Africa's currency, and its moves reflect domestic fiscal policy expectations and global dollar trends.

impacts.name: South African rand
impacts.why: Lower expected VAT would ease fiscal and inflation pressure, supporting demand for the rand.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

n2db2fd55df.why_moved: A report that the ANC may drop a VAT increase improved sentiment toward South African policy, while the dollar weakened on global markets.

n47fe307148.headline: Oando pipelines in Nigeria's oil-rich Bayelsa state hit by sabotage attacks
n47fe307148.summary: Nigerian oil producer Oando said three sabotage attacks targeted its pipelines in Bayelsa state over the past week.
n47fe307148.why: Oando is a Nigerian oil producer, and pipeline sabotage in the Niger Delta can cut crude output and raise operating costs.

n0b8e45581e.headline: African Markets – Factors to watch on April 14
n0b8e45581e.summary: Wall Street futures rallied in Asia after the White House exempted smartphones and computers from reciprocal US tariffs, though gains were limited.
n0b8e45581e.why: This daily preview lists scheduled data, company news and market moves that can influence African equity and currency markets.

ne0055d3a11.headline: Retailers warn Chinese sellers ‘dumping’ goods on UK marketplaces
ne0055d3a11.summary: The boss of Currys said there are early signs that stock meant for the US is already being diverted to the UK market.
ne0055d3a11.why: Diverted stock and low-priced sellers on online marketplaces can pressure UK retailers' prices and margins.

n63f8063b09.headline: U.K.'s Top Firms Brace for Turbulences Amid Cost Pressures, Tariff Fears, Survey Finds
n63f8063b09.summary: The UK's largest companies are tightening control over costs and hiring as they face economic headwinds, according to the latest Deloitte CFO survey.
n63f8063b09.why: CFO surveys give a read on corporate investment, hiring and cost plans, which signal the outlook for the wider economy.

n6f14bb4fd2.headline: South African businesses on edge as VAT hike looms
n6f14bb4fd2.summary: The National Treasury plans to raise value-added tax by one percentage point over two years from May 1 to bolster government revenue. Small businesses such as beverage makers say the increase could strain them.
n6f14bb4fd2.why: VAT is a consumption tax, and a rate increase affects consumer prices, household spending and government revenue.

naaf29d1218.headline: Morning Bid: Easter rising? Markets seek solace
naaf29d1218.summary: A late stock market rally on Wall Street on Friday extended into futures prices for a holiday-shortened week. Markets are weighing back-and-forth U.S. trade policy announcements from the past two days.
naaf29d1218.why: The S&P 500 and other US benchmarks reflect investor sentiment, which is sensitive to trade policy and tariff decisions.

nf10c5d7ca5.headline: China’s Xi says there are ‘no winners’ in tariff war as he visits South-east Asia
nf10c5d7ca5.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping said there are 'no winners' in the tariff war while visiting Southeast Asia. Donald Trump has paused some tariffs but kept 145 tariffs on China, the world's second-largest economy.
nf10c5d7ca5.why: China's tariff dispute with the US affects global trade flows, supply chains and the exports of manufacturers across Asia.

n33cea22380.headline: Access Bank gets final approval for Kenya's National Bank takeover
n33cea22380.summary: The Central Bank of Kenya and the National Treasury approved Nigerian lender Access Bank PLC's acquisition of the struggling National Bank, giving the deal final approval.
n33cea22380.why: Access Bank is a large Nigerian lender expanding across Africa, and its acquisitions reshape banking competition in the markets it enters.

ne3a26684f7.headline: Trump Weighs Tariff Relief for Auto Industry
ne3a26684f7.summary: President Donald Trump said he may temporarily ease 25% tariffs on foreign vehicles and parts to give carmakers time to shift production to the U.S. Automakers using parts from Canada and Mexico were also mentioned.
ne3a26684f7.why: Auto tariffs raise costs for carmakers that import vehicles and components, so changes to them affect global automotive supply chains and profit margins.
ne3a26684f7.why_moved: Investors reacted to a signal that tariffs on foreign vehicles and parts could be eased temporarily, which reduces expected cost pressure on carmakers.

n799af0ec95.headline: Stockholm stock exchange rises after tariff pause for electronics, OMXS30 index increases 1.8 percent
n799af0ec95.summary: The Stockholm stock exchange rose in a broad uptrend on Monday, with the OMXS30 index up 1.8%. The move followed a US tariff pause for electronics and tracked leading European exchanges.
n799af0ec95.why: The OMXS30 is the benchmark index of the most traded Swedish companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, so its moves reflect the health of Sweden's largest listed firms.

impacts.name: OMXS30
impacts.why: The index rose 1.8% in a broad market rally linked to the US tariff pause for electronics.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

n799af0ec95.why_moved: The index rallied after the US paused tariffs on electronics, improving sentiment in line with other leading European markets.

n574e104c9e.headline: Marex Group acquires UK cobalt trader Darton Commodities
n574e104c9e.summary: Marex Group has bought UK-based Darton Commodities, a trader of cobalt metal used in aerospace and military equipment, the financial services firm told Reuters.
n574e104c9e.why: Marex is a global financial services and commodities brokerage, so buying a specialist metals trader expands its physical commodities business. Cobalt is a key battery and superalloy metal.

ne8c391d544.headline: Trump says CBS and 60 Minutes should ‘pay a big price’ for going after him
ne8c391d544.summary: President Trump said CBS and 60 Minutes should 'pay a big price' for going after him. He called on Federal Communications Commission chairman Brendan Carr to impose maximum fines and punishment.
ne8c391d544.why: CBS is a major US broadcaster owned by Paramount Global, and FCC actions can carry financial penalties and affect broadcast licences. Government pressure on media companies is a regulatory risk for the sector.

n08a83acde0.headline: Argentina peso tumbles as Wall St cheers FX controls easing, IMF deal
n08a83acde0.summary: Argentina's peso fell 10% on Monday to near 1,200 per dollar after the government removed large parts of its currency and capital controls at the end of last week. The move is part of sealing a $20 billion deal with the IMF.
n08a83acde0.why: The peso is Argentina's currency, and capital controls limit how money can move in and out of the country. Easing them is a key step in the IMF-backed reform program that international investors watch closely.
n08a83acde0.why_moved: The government undid large parts of its currency and capital controls, which allowed the peso to reprice sharply. Wall Street welcomed the easing and the IMF deal.

nf8cb79bf11.headline: Trump administration freezes more than $2.2 billion after Harvard rejects its demands
nf8cb79bf11.summary: The government announced a freeze of more than $2.2 billion after Harvard refused demands it said would dictate what private universities can teach. The dispute centres on federal funding for the university.
nf8cb79bf11.why: Harvard is a large US research university that relies heavily on federal grants, so funding freezes affect its research budgets and the wider academic funding landscape.

n46ad752bc0.headline: Trump says tariffs will bring back manufacturing, but Wisconsin's labor shortage may stand in the way
n46ad752bc0.summary: Trump says tariffs will bring back manufacturing, but a labour shortage in Wisconsin may stand in the way, while shifting tariff rollouts make planning hard for manufacturers.
n46ad752bc0.why: Manufacturers rely on predictable trade policy and sufficient workers to plan investment, and labour shortages can limit output growth.

n13a102ec96.headline: AXIAN Telecom Secures $100M from EIB Global for Network Expansion in Madagascar and Tanzania : TechMoran
n13a102ec96.summary: AXIAN Telecom received a $100 million investment from EIB Global to expand its mobile broadband network in Madagascar and Tanzania.
n13a102ec96.why: AXIAN Telecom is a telecom infrastructure group operating mobile networks across Africa, and development-bank funding supports its capital spending.

n8f792df2ba.headline: The 1944 treaty under which Trump accuses Mexico of stealing water from Texas
n8f792df2ba.summary: Trump is threatening tariffs and sanctions until Mexico complies with the 1944 water treaty and gives Texas the water it is owed. The pact is 80 years old.
n8f792df2ba.why: Water-sharing disputes can escalate into trade measures, affecting cross-border commerce between the US and Mexico.

n585fe1746f.headline: Lawmakers fear AI data centers will drive up residents’ power bills
n585fe1746f.summary: US state lawmakers fear that growing electricity demand from artificial intelligence and data centers will push up residents' power bills. The concern is examined in a two-part States Newsroom series.
n585fe1746f.why: Data centers are large electricity consumers, and rising demand can affect utility costs, grid investment and regulatory decisions. This links AI infrastructure growth to power prices.

nd66a00caf8.headline: Tech tariff pivot helps Australian shares take a breath
nd66a00caf8.summary: Australian shares edged higher after a development in the US-China tariff dispute, with the White House carving out exemptions for technology products, according to the report.
nd66a00caf8.why: The ASX 200 is Australia's main benchmark index, and its heavy weighting in resources and financials makes it sensitive to global trade developments.
nd66a00caf8.why_moved: A White House carve-out in the US-China tariff dispute, covering tech, reduced trade worries and nudged Australian shares higher.

n10ee565a31.headline: Possible delay by Govt on minimum wage 'shameful' - ICTU
n10ee565a31.summary: ICTU General Secretary Owen Reidy called a possible government delay to the minimum wage 'shameful and unacceptable'.
n10ee565a31.why: Minimum wage levels shape labour costs for employers and household incomes, which feed into consumer spending in the economy.

n1762d49348.headline: Sony Hikes PlayStation 5 Price by 11% in Europe
n1762d49348.summary: Sony will raise PlayStation 5 prices in Europe, Britain, Australia and New Zealand, citing high inflation and fluctuating exchange rates. The disc-less model rises 11% to 499.99 euros from April 14.
n1762d49348.why: Sony Group is a Japanese electronics and entertainment conglomerate whose PlayStation consoles are a major part of its gaming business.

n53bf150100.headline: NZ BNZ services rises to 49.1, subdued despite hints of stabilization
n53bf150100.summary: New Zealand's services sector remained in contraction in March, with the BusinessNZ Performance of Services Index rising to 49.1 from 49.0. The reading is below the long-run average of 53.0.
n53bf150100.why: The services PMI gauges activity in the largest part of the New Zealand economy and informs Reserve Bank of New Zealand policy expectations. Readings below 50 signal contraction.

nf3c3ba1fce.headline: MAS eases Singapore dollar policy to help economy weather Trump’s tariff storm
nf3c3ba1fce.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore reduced the pace of the Singapore dollar's trade-weighted appreciation, its second such move in 2025. The step responds to easing inflation and rising growth risks from US tariffs.
nf3c3ba1fce.why: The MAS manages Singapore's currency rather than interest rates, so changes to the exchange-rate slope affect import prices and export competitiveness. It is a key policy signal for Asian FX traders.

impacts.name: Singapore dollar
impacts.why: The MAS reduced the pace of the currency's trade-weighted appreciation, which takes some upward pressure off the Singapore dollar.

n6b0aef3e00.headline: Trump’s trade war risks global meltdown, warns IMF
n6b0aef3e00.summary: The International Monetary Fund has warned that Donald Trump's trade war risks triggering a global financial meltdown.
n6b0aef3e00.why: The IMF is the Washington-based lender that monitors the global economy and publishes the World Economic Outlook forecasts used by investors.

nf2936eb949.headline: Big bite on spending swallows up hospitality businesses
nf2936eb949.summary: A record-high 9.4 per cent of food service and hospitality businesses shut their doors in the year to the reporting date. The article links the closures to heavy spending pressures.
nf2936eb949.why: Hospitality is a large employer and consumer-facing sector, so closures signal stress in household spending and small-business margins.

n8e2873e31f.headline: Sen. Warren Says Trump Tariffs Hurting Economy
n8e2873e31f.summary: Senator Elizabeth Warren said on CNN that uncertainty over how the tariffs will be enforced is stopping companies from making investments.
n8e2873e31f.why: Tariff policy shapes corporate capital spending and trade costs, which feed into growth and investor expectations.

n674e524211.headline: Caricom united against trade war
n674e524211.summary: The US push to rewrite international tariff and trade agreements may accelerate a Caribbean Community scheme towards regional integration, including freedom of movement.
n674e524211.why: Caricom is a regional bloc of Caribbean states whose trade and integration policies affect investment and commerce across the region.

n02a1025d2a.headline: Insurer profits boom to $6.1b after steep premium hikes
n02a1025d2a.summary: Insurance companies collectively banked $6.1 billion in annual profit after raising premiums and facing fewer significant weather events.
n02a1025d2a.why: Insurers' profitability depends on premium pricing and claims costs, which are sensitive to weather and catastrophe losses.

n9cecb386b1.headline: Ashmore hails ‘resilient’ emerging markets despite recent volatility
n9cecb386b1.summary: Emerging markets specialist Ashmore reported that total assets under management dipped by around 5%. The firm described emerging markets as resilient despite recent volatility.
n9cecb386b1.why: Ashmore is a London-based investment manager focused on emerging markets. Changes in assets under management affect its fee income and reflect investor flows into the asset class.

nb7c8d76348.headline: 'Inappropriate' for US to hit pharma amid talks - Harris
nb7c8d76348.summary: Tánaiste Simon Harris said it would be inappropriate for the US to hit the pharmaceutical sector with tariffs while it is negotiating with the EU on the trade relationship.
nb7c8d76348.why: Pharmaceuticals are a major export for Ireland and the EU, and US tariffs on the sector would directly affect drug makers' trade flows. Trade talks shape the terms of these tariffs.

nc1c2132bc9.headline: Ageas to buy UK insurance platform esure for $1.7 billion
nc1c2132bc9.summary: Ageas has agreed to buy British car and home insurer esure from Bain Capital for £1.3 billion, creating the third largest personal lines platform in the UK.
nc1c2132bc9.why: Ageas is a Belgian insurer with European operations, and personal lines insurance is a core business in motor and home cover that drives consolidation in the sector.

impacts.name: Ageas
impacts.why: Ageas is the buyer, taking on esure's UK car and home insurance book.

nbf875a89d6.headline: DAX-FLASH:  Significant recovery - Trump continues to row back on tariffs
nbf875a89d6.summary: The DAX is expected to open the shortened Easter trading week with a significant recovery. The move reflects a further easing of global customs disputes, according to MarketScreener.
nbf875a89d6.why: The DAX is Germany's benchmark stock index of 40 major companies, and it is sensitive to trade policy because of Germany's export exposure.

n1b58e55b70.headline: Tech Industry's Exemption From 125 Percent 'Reciprocal' Tariff Will Only Last "A Month Or Two" As Products Like The iPhone Will Be Subject To A "Special Focus Type Of Tariff"
n1b58e55b70.summary: Apple and other tech companies' exemption from the 125% reciprocal tariff will last only a month or two, according to the report. Products such as the iPhone are expected to face a special tariff.
n1b58e55b70.why: Apple designs the iPhone and relies heavily on manufacturing in Asia, so tariff changes directly affect its costs and margins.

impacts.why: A special tariff on iPhones would raise the cost of imported devices made abroad.

n138904b24e.headline: Ringgit ends slightly higher against greenback amid lower DXY
n138904b24e.summary: The ringgit closed slightly higher against the US dollar as the US Dollar Index declined, according to an analyst cited in the report.
n138904b24e.why: The ringgit is Malaysia's currency, and its moves against the dollar affect import costs, foreign investment and exporters.

impacts.name: US Dollar Index
impacts.why: A falling dollar index is the stated reason for the ringgit's gain.

na187a5db27.headline: Apple takes top spot for first-quarter smartphone sales, data shows
na187a5db27.summary: Apple took the top spot for global smartphone sales in the first quarter, helped by the iPhone 16e launch and strong demand in Japan and India, Counterpoint Research data showed.
na187a5db27.why: Apple is the US maker of the iPhone, one of the world's largest smartphone vendors. Quarterly shipment rankings are a key indicator of demand for its flagship products.

impacts.name: Apple
impacts.why: Top global smartphone ranking in the quarter reflects strong iPhone demand.

n0ca566d765.headline: Bank of Canada Rate Announcement Won
n0ca566d765.summary: The Bank of Canada is set to announce its latest interest rate decision on April 16, as many Canadian households face rising debt and living costs.
n0ca566d765.why: The Bank of Canada sets the country's benchmark policy rate, which influences mortgage costs, bond yields and the Canadian dollar. Its decisions are closely watched by investors.

n12816bc323.headline: Green meters push PESCO toward bankruptcy
n12816bc323.summary: The Express Tribune reports that the introduction of green meters is pushing PESCO, the Pakistani power distributor, toward bankruptcy.
n12816bc323.why: PESCO is a state-owned electricity distribution company in Pakistan, and financial distress at utilities affects power sector debt and energy supply.

na404a2fee3.headline: China's Xi Jinping says there are no winners in a tariff war as he visits Southeast Asia
na404a2fee3.summary: Xi Jinping said no one wins a trade war as he began a diplomatic tour of Southeast Asia with a trip to Vietnam.
na404a2fee3.why: China is the world's second-largest economy, and its trade policy shapes global supply chains and tariff negotiations.

ncc0bbd65e1.headline: BoJ's Ueda: US tariffs add downside risks to Japan through various channels
ncc0bbd65e1.summary: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda warned that recently imposed US tariffs are likely to exert downward pressure on the global and Japanese economies through various channels.
ncc0bbd65e1.why: The Bank of Japan sets monetary policy for the world's fourth-largest economy, and its guidance shapes yen and Japanese government bond expectations. Tariffs affect Japanese exporters.

n5c85bf46f0.headline: Indonesia eyes US oil, gas investment amid tariff dispute
n5c85bf46f0.summary: Investment in oil and gas could be a potential entry point for Indonesian companies in the United States, according to a deputy investment minister. The comments come amid a tariff dispute.
n5c85bf46f0.why: Indonesia is a Southeast Asian energy producer and exporter, and its firms investing abroad can shape bilateral trade and energy flows. Tariff disputes affect the terms of cross-border deals.

n9ea1a71357.headline: 3 MoUs, 1 pact inked during Prabowo's Jordan visit
n9ea1a71357.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and King Abdullah II of Jordan witnessed the signing of three memoranda of understanding and one cooperation agreement.
n9ea1a71357.why: Bilateral agreements between governments can open trade and investment channels between the two countries.
